issues.description: GKE detection via 'gke-' name-prefix is a brittle heuristic, not a real managed-by-GKE property.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flag this. A user-named VM 'gke-bastion' becomes MANUAL; a real GKE node with custom naming becomes FAIL. The actual fact lives in instance labels/metadata (goog-gke-node) or managed-instance-group ancestry. Either query that label, or document the heuristic explicitly and accept its limits.

issues.description: Check identity is ambiguous: PR title says 'multiple_network_interfaces' while file/dir/metadata say 'single_network_interface'.
issues.detail: PR title, description, and CHANGELOG framing reference detecting multiple NICs, but class, directory, and metadata use 'single_network_interface'. A reader cannot tell whether PASS means 'has one' or 'has many'. Pick one name and apply it consistently across title, CHANGELOG, metadata, directory, and class.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently returns PASS, violating the implied postcondition.
issues.detail: When interface_count == 0, status remains the default PASS while status_extended says 'no network interfaces'. A VM with zero NICs is not a single-NIC VM — it's an anomalous state. Emit MANUAL or an explicit error rather than silently asserting compliance. Also untested.

issues.description: Tri-state MANUAL output contradicts metadata and PR description (PASS/FAIL only).
issues.detail: The code emits PASS, FAIL, and MANUAL, but metadata and the PR description describe only PASS/FAIL semantics. This drift between policy, presentation, and declared behavior will bite later. Align the metadata, docstring, and code on one story about what statuses this check can emit.

issues.description: Mutable default '[]' on Pydantic network_interfaces field; prefer Field(default_factory=list).
issues.detail: network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = [] is consistent with the file's existing style and Pydantic copies defaults per-instance, but the idiom reads as a Python mutable-default footgun. Prefer Field(default_factory=list) for clarity and forward-compatibility while the field is new.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model strips fields needed to distinguish real cross-boundary bridges from benign multi-NIC.
issues.detail: Modeling NICs as {name, network, subnetwork} discards accessConfigs/natIP, alias IP ranges, stack type, and the full network URL. The check can't then ask the interesting question of whether NICs cross trust boundaries, and short-name collisions across shared VPCs become indistinguishable. Keep the value richer; classifier stays pure.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a check that works for happy paths but is under-reasoned at the edges. Three issues draw unanimous concern: the GKE carve-out uses a brittle name-prefix heuristic instead of the actual managed-by-GKE label/metadata; the check's identity is ambiguous between 'single' and 'multiple' across title, CHANGELOG, and code; and the zero-interface branch silently returns PASS in violation of its implied postcondition. Secondary concerns include MANUAL status drift from declared PASS/FAIL semantics, a thin NetworkInterface value model that drops the fields needed to detect real boundary-crossing, and a mutable-default Pydantic field. Verdict: revise before merge — align naming, replace the prefix heuristic with label-based detection, and make the zero-NIC case explicit with a covering test.
